title: Quantum Fourier-Product State Preparation
summary: With roughly uniform Fourier coefficients, equality filtering needs on the order of two raised to n over two queries; a competitive generic algorithm for the general case remains unknown.

formal_statement.body: For Boolean functions $f,g:\mathbb{F}_2^n\to\{-1,1\}$, given query access to $g$ and a black box preparing the Fourier-coefficient state $\sum_x \widehat{f}(x)\lvert x\rangle$, determine whether there is a competitive generic quantum algorithm that prepares a state whose amplitudes are proportional to $\widehat{g}(x)\widehat{f}(x)$ for every $x$. A generic equality-filtering method can achieve this with $O(2^{n/2})$ queries when the Fourier coefficients are distributed approximately uniformly, but the unresolved task is to obtain a competitive algorithm for the general setting.

scope.domain: Quantum state preparation from Fourier coefficients of Boolean functions over binary vector spaces.
assumptions: Query access to g and black-box access to the Fourier-coefficient state of f.
Approximate uniformity of the Fourier coefficients for the stated equality-filtering bound.
parameters: n: dimension of the binary input space
f and g: Boolean functions defining the supplied and target Fourier amplitudes
scope.unresolved_remainder: Determine whether a competitive generic quantum algorithm can prepare the state with amplitudes proportional to the pointwise product of the two Fourier spectra in the general setting.

citations.label: Quantum Linear Key-recovery Attacks Using the QFT

progress.summary: The source states this as Problem 1, then describes equality filtering as a baseline under approximately uniform Fourier coefficients. It says that no competitive generic algorithm is known more generally.
citation_labels: André Schrottenloher et al., Quantum Linear Key-recovery Attacks Using the QFT
